label: t6-flyingfish-data
topic: Track 6 data and reproducibility: flying-fish glide energy certificate
summary: Downloaded Deng 2019 (Zenodo, md5 matches the record) and Makiguchi 2013 (publisher open PDF); read Park and Choi 2010 and Daane 2021 Data S1 from the project's cached copies because both refuse automated download. repro.py ran 67 checks: 65 reproduce. Every headline number of the scout and design agents reproduces (energy-bound ranges 22.3/50.1/89.1 m, vmin 9.85 m/s, stall-floor bounds 0.65/28.5/67.5 m, 49 flying fish with pectoral/SL 0.406-0.823, 14 adults 0.656-0.757, 3 above 0.76, 2 above 0.79). The data overturn three readings: (1) Deng's abstract 45.4 m and 13.2 m come from two different runs (alpha0=0 deg, gamma=25 deg gives 45.4 m in 3.5 s; 13.2 m is the apex of the alpha0=10 deg, gamma=40 deg run, whose range peak is 41.5 m), and every run launches at a fixed 20 m/s, so the design's P1 launch-speed premise (v0 >= 16.1 m/s) is satisfied by construction; (2) on those Deng runs the distance is 0.43-0.47 of the no-stall-floor energy bound (0.56-0.61 with the stall floor), inside the design's P2 window [0.30, 1.00], but this is Deng's own quasi-steady model, not an independent flight; (3) Makiguchi 2013 reports no per-leap airborne time (its 'duration' is the tail-acceleration phase), so design prediction P3 is untestable from this paper. Also found: the project's glide-data.csv says the Makiguchi mean length 325.0 mm and mass 227.7 g are 'over 13 fish'; Table 1 shows they are the mean of the ten 2010 fish only (all 13 give 312.8 mm, 221.6 g).
lay_summary: Earlier helpers claimed numbers about how far a flying fish can glide. We downloaded the original papers and measurements and redid the arithmetic with a short program anyone can rerun. Almost every number came out the same. A fish gliding is like a cyclist coasting off a hill: the speed it starts with can be traded for distance, but only down to the speed at which its wings stop holding it up. When we opened the computer-simulation paper, we found its two headline figures, a 45.4 m glide and a 13.2 m climb, came from two different simulated flights, and that every simulated flight started at 20 metres per second. We also found the aquarium paper never records how long each leap lasted, so one planned test cannot be done from it.

glossary.plain: How many metres a glider moves forward for each metre it drops; higher is a better glider.
The slowest speed at which the wings can still hold the weight up.
Body weight divided by wing area, in newtons per square metre; heavier for the same wing means a higher stall speed.
A ceiling on glide distance set by the launch height plus the launch speed turned into height.
A computer model that tracks a flyer's forward, up-down and pitching motion in a flat slice.
Computer simulation of air flowing around a shape.
A fingerprint of a file; any change to the file changes the fingerprint.
The large side fin behind the gill cover, used as a wing in flying fish.
Body length from snout to the end of the backbone, not counting the tail fin.
The angle above horizontal at which the fish leaves the water.

Deng's launch speed is fixed at 20 m/s in all 3-DOF runs, at initial angle of attack 0 or 10 deg and path angles 10-40 deg. The design's open question about 'launch conditions not yet recorded' is answered.
findings.evidence_quote: The take-off speed is fixed at 20 m s-1 for all the calculations, and two initial angles of attack

findings.claim: Deng's abstract combines two runs: 45.4 m (alpha0 = 0, gamma = 25 deg, endurance 3.5 s, max height of that series 12.5 m at gamma = 40) and 13.2 m (alpha0 = 10 deg series, gamma = 40 deg), where that series' range peak is 41.5 m in 3.47 s. The design's 'one trajectory with 45.4 m distance and 13.2 m height' is not what the paper reports.
findings.evidence_quote: distance and its endurance are 41.5 m and 3.47 s, respectively

findings.claim: Deng abstract states 45.4 m distance and 13.2 m height, CLmax 1.03 and L/Dmax 4.7 (matches scout).
findings.evidence_quote: can achieve a distance up to 45.4 m, and reach a height of 13.2 m

findings.claim: Deng's model C: body mass 0.09 kg, pectoral wing area A1 = 154 cm2, pelvic A2 = 16.37 cm2, wing loading 57.3 N/m2 (reproduced: 0.09 x 9.80665 / 0.0154 = 57.31). Deng's force coefficients use A1 only, whereas Park and Choi's use A1+A2+A3, so the two CLmax values (1.03 and 0.78) are not on the same area.
findings.source: Deng 2019 PDF section 2.1 and section 3.1; Park and Choi 2010 cached PDF, reference-area paragraph
findings.evidence_quote: resulting in a wing loading of 57.3 Nm-2

findings.claim: Stall speed of Deng's model C from its own numbers (rho 1.225 unverified background, CLmax 1.03 on A1): 9.53 m/s, below the 20 m/s launch.
Design prediction P1 reading: all Deng runs launch at 20 m/s, so apex <= v0^2/2g = 20.39 m holds for 12.5 m and 13.2 m, and the premise 'v0 >= 16.1 m/s' holds by construction rather than as a test.

Design prediction P2 on Deng's 3-DOF runs: distance / (4.7 x 400 / 19.62 = 95.8 m) = 0.474 for 45.4 m and 0.433 for 41.5 m; with the stall floor (bound 74.0 m) 0.613 and 0.560. All inside the design window [0.30, 1.00]; none above 1. Caveat: this is Deng's own quasi-steady model with CFD coefficients, so it is a consistency check, not an independent flight.
Deng computed aerodynamic coefficients at a fixed 10 m/s (Re 2.6e4) while the fish takes off at 20 m/s; the paper itself calls the 3-DOF result preliminary.
findings.evidence_quote: a fixed velocity of 10 m s-1 is considered in our simulations for the aerodynamic coefficients

findings.claim: Makiguchi 2013 abstract: estimated leap speed 3.9 to 5.2 m/s, 38.7 to 51.5% of earlier maxima; body text 3.87 to 5.15 m/s from stride length 0.6-0.8 L and stroke frequency 21.2 Hz. Recomputing 0.6/0.8 x 0.308 m x 21.2 Hz gives 3.92-5.22 m/s, within rounding of L.
findings.evidence_quote: the flying fish were estimated to leap from the water surface at speeds of 3.9 to 5.2 m s-1

findings.claim: Makiguchi 2013 does not report airborne time per leap. 'airborne' appears twice, both in a figure caption describing pitch; every 'duration' counted (22 with a preceding word, 17 'acceleration duration') is the tail-acceleration phase. Design prediction P3 is therefore 'cannot test' from this paper.
findings.source: repro.py checks Mak-duration-keyword and Mak-airborne-keyword on the fetched PDF
findings.evidence_quote: Once airborne, the fish undergoes significant

findings.claim: Makiguchi Table 1: 13 fish (A-M), column sums 10 leaps and 23 burst-swimming events. The printed 'Average 325.0 +- 11.4 mm, 227.7 +- 19.8 g' equals the mean and SD of the ten 2010 fish A-J only (recomputed 325.0 +- 11.4; 227.7 +- 19.8). The mean of all 13 is 312.8 mm and 221.6 g. The project's glide-data.csv note 'mean fork length 325.0 +- 11.4 mm and mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 fish' is therefore wrong on the count.
findings.source: repro.py (Mak-table1-*) on the fetched PDF; project note from delphisci/physics/glide-data.csv

findings.claim: Makiguchi text says 9 fish (30.8 +- 3.1 cm) were used for leap speed; Table 1 lists 8 fish with at least one leap (mean fork length 30.5 cm). Not reconciled.

Park and Choi Table 2, model L3: L/Dmax 4.37 at 0 deg, CLmax 0.78 at 35 deg, CDmin 0.055 at -10 deg (matches scout/design). Coefficients use reference area A1+A2+A3. Table 1 L3 areas 6377, 1837, 4474 mm2 (sum 12688); aspect ratio 261^2/6377 = 10.68 matches the printed 10.7.
Park and Choi report the drag reduction by ground effect as 9% (solid surface, r about 0.21) and 14% (water surface, r about 0.33) for model L3.
findings.source: cached Park and Choi PDF, ground-effect section
findings.evidence_quote: whereas the of 9% and 14% were from the body and wing for model L3

findings.claim: Park and Choi body masses are printed to 0.01 kg (L3 = 0.06 kg), so the stall floor carries a rounding band: if L3's true mass is 0.055-0.065 kg, wing loading is 42.5-50.3 N/m2 and vmin is 9.43-10.26 m/s, not the single 9.85 m/s. This matters for the design's verdict (a) because 10 m/s sits inside that band.

Scout energy bound reproduces: range <= (L/D) v^2/2g with L/D 4.37 gives 22.27 m at 10, 50.11 m at 15, 89.09 m at 20 m/s; 14.98 m/s for 50 m; 16.09 m/s to reach 13.2 m (scout: 22.3, 50.1, 89.1, 15.0, 16.1).

Design stall-floor numbers reproduce: vmin 9.85 m/s (vmin^2 97.10), bounds 0.65/28.49/67.47 m (delta 0) and 0.75/33.12/78.45 m (delta 0.14), launch speed for 50 m 17.93 and 17.03 m/s; Cheilopogon vmin 12.50 and 14.36 m/s, airborne time 0.50 s, reach 2.37 m.
L3 wing loading is 46.39 N/m2 with g = 9.81 (design) and 46.37 with g = 9.80665 (registry band); both reproduce.

Daane 2021 Data S1 sheet A (xlsx, 109 specimens): 49 flying fish with pectoral/SL min 0.406, max 0.823, median 0.687; 60 other beloniforms with max 0.3884; 14 flying fish with SL >= 15 cm span 0.656-0.757; 3 exceed 0.76 and 2 exceed 0.79, all Hirundichthys rondeleti with SL 2.4-6.04 cm. All reproduce the scout. Sheet column H equals F/E on every row.
In the sheet, specimen 1 has pelvic/SL = 2.4e-16 (formula artefact) while the true pelvic/SL is 6.9/23 = 0.30; the pelvic column of the sheet should not be used without recomputing.
findings.source: xlsx cell I2 and G2/E2 (sheet 'A - fin measurement')

could_not_find: Automatic re-download of Daane 2021 Data S1: the PMC URL returns a 1,816-byte JavaScript proof-of-work page, Europe PMC and the Cell CDN return 403/500. Numbers come from the project's cached copy of the Cell Press supplement (mmc2.xlsx, sha256 above); its origin is the project's README claim, not something I re-fetched. I did not bypass the challenge.

Park and Choi 2010 full text from the publisher: HTTP 403. Values come from the project's cached PDF. pdftotext scrambles the Table 1 row labels, so label-to-value pairing for A1/A2/A3 rests on the aspect-ratio check (261^2/6377 = 10.68) and the repo's reading, not on text alignment.
Deng's trajectory curves (Figures 8 and 9) are plots; I could not read per-run values beyond the numbers in the text (45.4 m, 3.5 s, 12.5 m; 41.5 m, 3.47 s, 13.2 m). I did not estimate others.
Per-leap airborne time in Makiguchi 2013: not reported; P3 is untestable from this paper.
No public raw glide-trajectory dataset (as the scout found); every field distance remains second-hand.
Air density 1.225 kg/m3 and g are unverified background used in all vmin numbers.
No Lean build was run (not needed for the data task); the wrapper glide_energy_range_rules_out is not in the application repo's Delphi/*.lean.
The cached CSV extract and xlsx came from the project, so independent reproduction of Daane covers the parsing and arithmetic, not the publisher's file identity.
recommendations: Correct the design's P1/P2 text: Deng launches at a fixed 20 m/s and the abstract's two figures are different runs; restate P2 as distance/bound = 0.43-0.47 (0.56-0.61 with the stall floor) and say it is a model self-consistency check.
Mark P3 'cannot test from Makiguchi 2013' now and look for a source with airborne times, or drop it.
Carry the Park and Choi mass rounding into the certificate: use vmin as an interval 9.43-10.26 m/s, since the 10 m/s launch verdict (a) sits inside it.
Fix the 'over 13 fish' note in the project's glide-data.csv: the mean is of ten fish.
Put Deng's CLmax 1.03 (area A1 only) and Park and Choi's 0.78 (area A1+A2+A3) on one reference area before mixing them in any certificate.
